description: Manual STRIDE analysis of an intentionally insecure REST API application. Performed by a security analyst reviewing the application architecture, source code, and live traffic.

threats.description: Server allows requests from ANY origin (*), enabling cross-site attacks and data theft.
threats.mitigation: Restrict CORS to specific trusted origins.

threats.description: JWT signature not properly verified; tampered tokens are accepted by the server.
threats.mitigation: Enforce strict JWT signature verification using a secure algorithm.

threats.description: Unsanitized user input passed directly into SQL queries allows injection attacks.
threats.mitigation: Use parameterized queries and prepared statements.

threats.description: User-supplied input is reflected in responses without encoding, enabling script injection.
threats.mitigation: Sanitize and encode all user inputs; apply Content-Security-Policy.

threats.description: Application lacks immutable audit logging; actions can be performed without a traceable record.
threats.mitigation: Implement tamper-evident, append-only audit logs with timestamps and user context.

threats.description: Insufficient path validation allows attackers to read arbitrary files from the filesystem.
threats.mitigation: Validate and canonicalize file paths; restrict access to a safe root directory.

threats.description: Database passwords and API keys are stored in plaintext within configuration files.
threats.mitigation: Move secrets to environment variables or a secrets manager.

threats.description: Application accepts trivially weak passwords (e.g., '123456'), exposing accounts to brute-force.
threats.mitigation: Enforce strong password policies requiring length, complexity, and uniqueness.
